settings.generalDescription: How Nixus looks and behaves on this computer.
settings.themeDescription: Follow your system setting, or pick one.
settings.languageDescription: Changes every label in the app.
settings.hideAmountsDescription: Every dollar figure starts hidden. Useful in a café or when you share a screen. You can still flip it any time from the sidebar.
settings.trayTitle: Reminders only work while Nixus is running
settings.trayDescription: Closing the window quits Nixus completely, so reminders stop until you open it again. Staying in the menu bar isn't built yet, so there's nothing to turn on here.
settings.readingDescription: Nixus uses an AI service to read your statements and sort the transactions. You supply the key, and it's the only part of Nixus that uses the internet.
settings.readingReassuranceBody: Budgets, accounts, net worth, and manual entry never touch the network. If you'd rather not set up a key, you can type transactions in yourself.
settings.providerDescription: Pick the one you already have an account with.
settings.providerBedrockDescription: Reads statements with Claude, using your AWS keys.
settings.providerOpenaiDescription: Reads statements with GPT, using your OpenAI key.
settings.keychainNote: Stored in your computer's keychain, never in the Nixus database.
settings.secretKeyNote: Also in your keychain. Nixus can't show it again once saved.
settings.regionNote: The one closest to you keeps things quick.
settings.regionRequired: Enter a region, for example ca-central-1.
settings.whatGetsSentBody: When you import, that image or PDF goes to the service you picked above and the transactions come back. Your budget, balances, accounts, and net worth are never sent.
settings.rememberMerchantsBody: Kept on this computer only. Next month Nixus already knows that METRO is Groceries, so there's less to review each time. It's always on — there's no switch for it yet.
settings.yourDataDescription: Everything lives in one file on this computer. There's no cloud copy, so backups are yours to keep.
settings.backupSaveBody: Writes a single file you can put on a USB stick or in your own cloud folder.
settings.dataLocationUnknown: Nixus doesn't report the file path yet.
settings.restoreWarningBody: Whatever is in Nixus now is written over by the backup file. Save a copy first if you're unsure.
settings.restoreBody: Nixus asks you to pick the file before anything changes.
settings.exportOwnershipLine: Your data is yours — you should be able to export any of it to a spreadsheet at any time.
settings.exportUnavailableBody: A backup copy is the only way out today, and that's a database file rather than a spreadsheet. Until export lands, the honest answer is that you'd have to retype.
settings.templateExportTitle: Save your budget as a template
settings.templateExportBody: Creates a file with your group and category names only — every dollar amount is left out, so you can share it safely.
settings.templateImportBody: Adds the template's groups and categories to your budget. Groups you already have are skipped, and every new category starts at $1.00 so you can set your own targets.

settings.aboutDescription: What Nixus is, and what it isn't.
settings.aboutLimitLocal: Your data stays on this computer. There's no account and nothing to sign up for.
settings.aboutLimitNoBank: Nixus doesn't connect to your bank. You upload statements yourself.
settings.aboutLimitSingleUser: One person's finances per install. There's no household sharing.
settings.aboutLimitNotAdvice: A tracking tool — not tax, legal, or investment advice.
settings.aboutLimitEarly: Things change and some things break between releases.
settings.aboutStorageBody: Nixus adds no encryption of its own. Whatever your operating system already encrypts on this disk is what protects the file.

onboarding.limitEarlyBody: Things will change and some things will break. Telling me what confused you is the most useful thing you can do.
